Friction Wedge Inspection: What a Dimensional Report Cannot Prove

Separate casting and dimensional acceptance from evidence about the complete suspension system when qualifying a new wedge supply.

November 14, 2026 · Quality · Ma'anshan Railwheel Industrial Technology Co., Ltd.

Identify the limit of the inspection decision

A dimensional report can demonstrate conformity to specified measured characteristics. It cannot, by itself, establish the behavior of a complete freight bogie. Incoming inspection and system validation are separate controls. Treating a passed part report as permission for an unapproved design change assigns the receiving inspector a decision that belongs to the responsible engineering authority.

Choose characteristics from the actual drawing

The inspection plan should identify functional faces, datums, contact profiles, material requirements and specified surface conditions. Require results that map to drawing references. A report of length, width and mass may be accurate yet omit the contact characteristics that matter to the application. If a functional gauge is specified, record its control and the exact feature it evaluates.

Engineering principle: inspection has a defined observation boundary

Consider a dimensional report that checks external width at selected locations. Its observation boundary is those characteristics under the specified measurement conditions. Increasing the sample quantity improves coverage of that defined check; it does not turn the measurement into an assessment of every contact profile, material property or dynamic response. The correct response to missing characteristics is to improve the inspection definition, not simply request more copies of the same report. First establish what needs to be demonstrated, then choose the method, coverage and acceptance authority appropriate to that requirement.

Keep manufacturing examinations specific

Where material tests or examinations are required, define the method, coverage, acceptance criteria and traceability. Do not add a list of familiar test names without determining their relevance to the material and design. Conversely, a supplier's standard inspection routine should not replace additional contractual requirements. Close any difference during quotation, before castings or machining begin.

Evaluate a changed supply route separately

A different casting source, material condition, facing system or design revision can affect the qualification baseline. Ask the supplier to declare such changes and identify the evidence it proposes. Existing reports need a documented applicability review; simply attaching them to a new quotation does not establish coverage. The buyer should identify who can accept the qualification argument and whether additional evidence is required.

Make release records usable after delivery

The report should identify the part and revision, batch or other required identifier, inspection dates, results and disposition. Package labels and the packing list must connect to that identity. Retain nonconformance and concession records with the affected items. A later maintenance investigation needs to know what was supplied and accepted, not merely that the supplier once held a quality certificate.

Application scenario

Illustrative scenario: a new bidder offers a wedge with a complete dimensional report but a different construction from the approved item. Procurement records the dimensional evidence without treating it as substitution approval. Engineering reviews the construction difference and the required system evidence before deciding whether the proposed item can enter the approved parts list.

Technical review checklist

Checks to define in the project documentation
Review itemRequired definitionPurpose
Dimension reportMeasured drawing characteristicsDoes not approve a new suspension design
Material evidenceSpecified material requirementsMust link to the supplied scope
QualificationDefined design or process baselineRequires applicability review
ReleaseIdentity and dispositionMust follow the accepted baseline

Frequently asked questions

Does 100-percent dimensional inspection prove interchangeability?

No. Inspection coverage does not expand the characteristics or system behavior the inspection actually evaluates.

Can an old qualification report support a new batch?

Only where its applicability is established and the current production acceptance requirements are also met.
